learningObjective: Distinguish instruction-level, data-level and thread-level parallelism, and identify architectural mechanisms exposing each form.

canonicalClaims.claim: ILP, DLP and TLP are three orthogonal forms of parallelism that modern systems combine: ILP within a core's pipeline, DLP within SIMD lanes / SIMT warps, and TLP across cores or independent thread streams.
conditions: Comparison across general-purpose parallel architectures (CPUs and GPUs).
nonImplications: Does not imply the three are mutually exclusive.
Does not imply exploiting one always benefits another; there are tradeoffs (e.g., larger issue windows may cost area for wider SIMD).

misconceptions.claim: A program exhibits only one form of parallelism at a time; the architecture must choose which to exploit.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Modern GPUs combine DLP (SIMT), TLP (many warps), and ILP (per-thread pipeline) simultaneously.

misconceptions.claim: SIMT is a form of TLP because each lane has its own thread ID.
misconceptions.whyWrong: SIMT is primarily a DLP mechanism (same instruction across lanes); TLP within a GPU is expressed across warps and blocks.

misconceptions.claim: ILP is only relevant to CPUs, not GPUs.
misconceptions.whyWrong: GPU threads execute pipelined instructions; per-thread ILP (independent instructions in the stream) still matters for MMA/scalar dispatch.
misconceptions.sourceOrEvidence: HP6 ILP chapter and NVIDIA architecture whitepapers

implementationFacts: ILP mechanisms: OoO, register renaming, wide issue, pipelining.
DLP mechanisms: SIMD registers/instructions, SIMT warps.
TLP mechanisms: multi-core, SMT/hyperthreading, GPU warps/blocks.
performanceScenarios: CPU BLAS kernels exploit SIMD (DLP) and multi-core (TLP) plus OoO (ILP) simultaneously.
GPU GEMM combines SIMT (DLP), warp-level pipelines (ILP), and many active warps (TLP for latency hiding).
